caseno: Civil Petition For Leave To Appeal No. 307 of 1995
lawyer:
Mr. Syed Mahmud Hossain, Advocate (appeared with leave of the Court), instructed by Mr. Md. Nawab Ali, Advocate-on-Record ----- for the Petitioners. 
Respondent: Not represented.
parties:
Md. Nizamuddin and others ----- Plaintiff - Petitioners
Vs.
People Republic of Bangladesh ----- Defendant-Respondent
full_judgment: Muhammad Abdur Rouf, J: The plaintiffs have sought for leave to appeal against the judgment and order dated 12 February 1995 passed by a Single Bench of the High Court Division in making the Rule absolute, issued in Civil Revision No. 185 of 1989 (Comilla), renumbered as Civil Revision 4343 of 1991 (Dhaka) and setting aside the judgment and decree passed on 15 February 1989 by the Additional District Judge, Noakhali, allowing Title Appeal No. 41 of 1980 and reversing thereby the judgment and decree passed on 29 January 1980 by the Subordinate Judge, Additional Court, Noakhali, dismissing O.C. Suit No of 1974. In the suit the present petitioners sought for declaration of their title to 9.14 acres of land stating inter alia that the suit land originally belonged to Ex-rent-receiver Abhoy Chandra Chowdhury and others under whom Ahmedulla and others had a tenancy right which ultimately devolved upon their heirs Mujibul Huq and others. Petitioners predecessor Syed Mia took settlement of the said land from Mojibul Huq and others by executing a Kabuliyat on 13th Ashwin 1362 B.S. corresponding to 18 September 1955. He excavated a tank therein and planted bamboo clump thereon. Syed Mia also got his name recorded in respect of 8.15 acres out of the suit land in M.R.R. Khatian No. 1959, prepared in 1960 and paid Tent to the Government thereunder. The said land was subsequently recorded in Diara Khatian No. 744 in the name of Syed Mia. Upon an objection raised by the Government the same was wrongly recorded in the Khas Khatian of the Government. During pendency of the suit the original plaintiff died and then the present petitioners proceeded with the suit as the substituted plaintiffs. The Government contested the suit by filing written statement denying plaintiffs right, title and possession in the suit land. Defence case is that the rent-receiving-interest of Abhoy Chandra and others was auction purchased by Bhalua Estate on 22-11-1899 AD, in Rent Execution Case No. 30 of 1899 in pursuance of the decree passed in Rent Suit No. 10 of 1898. The sale was confirmed on 13-3-1900. Bhalua Estate got possession therein on 13-6-1900. During preparation of CS. Khatian 1297.78 acres including the suit land was recorded in Khas Khatian of Bhalua Estate in Plot Nos. 1-9. Part of the auction purchased land on being diluviated had been under water for about 25 years and recorded in the year 1959-60 in the Khas Khatian of the Government. The original plaintiff (since dead) collusively made a Diara Khatian in his name and upon an objection filed by the Government the said land was correctly recorded in the Khas Khatian of the Government and that Syed Miah did not acquire any right, title and interest in the suit land on the basis of the collusive unilateral Kabullyat. The trial Court dismissed the suit holding, inter alia that the plaintiffs could not prove that Ahmedullah and others had any jote right under the ex-rent receiver Abhoy Chandra Chowdhury and that the plaintiffs Kabuhyat did not create any right in respect of the suit land. The plaintiffs preferred an appeal there against and the lower appellate Court allowed the appeal and reversed the decree of the trial Court and decreed the suit holding inter alia that the plaintiffs Kabuliyat had been acted upon long before the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act came into operation in the district of Noakhali and that the Government recognised the plaintiffs tenancy right in 1963 accepting rent in M.R.R. Khatian. Against which the Government moved the High Court Division in revision and got the Rule. By the impugned judgment and order the High Court Division has set aside the decree of the lower appellate Court and restored that of the trial Court and thereby the suit has been dismissed.
